draft.title: The Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient
card: Lorenz curve
A graph of the cumulative share of income against the cumulative share of households, ranked from poorest to richest.
Line of equality
A straight diagonal line. Along it, every 10% of households holds 10% of income. The further the Lorenz curve bows below this line, the more unequal the distribution.
Gini coefficient
A number that sums up the gap between the Lorenz curve and the line of equality. It runs from 0 (everyone has the same income) to 1 (one household holds all the income).
A higher Gini coefficient means a more unequal distribution. The Gini coefficient can be compared across countries or across years, but it does not show which households are rich or poor.
draft.remember: A Lorenz curve bowed further from the diagonal means a higher Gini coefficient and more inequality.

a.q: A country's Lorenz curve moves closer to the line of equality over ten years. What has happened to its Gini coefficient and its income inequality?
opts: The Gini coefficient fell and inequality fell
The Gini coefficient fell and inequality rose
The Gini coefficient rose and inequality fell
The Gini coefficient rose and inequality rose
a.why: A curve closer to the line of equality means incomes are more evenly spread. That gives a lower Gini coefficient. The tempting option is a rise in the Gini coefficient, but a higher number means a bigger gap from the line and more inequality.
a.clue: The line of equality has a Gini coefficient of 0.

b.q: In Country X, the poorest 50% of households hold 20% of income. In Country Y, the poorest 50% hold 35% of income. What can be said about the two countries?
opts: Country Y's Lorenz curve is closer to the line of equality
Country X has the lower Gini coefficient of the two
Country Y has the higher Gini coefficient of the two
Country X's Lorenz curve is closer to the line of equality
b.why: At the 50% mark, Country Y's curve is higher, so it sits closer to the line of equality. This gives Y a lower Gini coefficient and a more even distribution. The tempting wrong idea is that a higher share for the poor means a higher Gini coefficient, but the reverse is true.
b.clue: A higher point on the graph for the poorest half means a curve nearer the diagonal.

a.best: The Gini coefficient fell and inequality fell

b.best: Country Y's Lorenz curve is closer to the line of equality

problems.detail: A single point (the poorest 50%) does not fix a whole Lorenz curve. Curves can cross, so Y's curve is only certainly closer to the line of equality at the 50% mark, and Y's Gini is not guaranteed to be lower. The why still states flatly that Y has a lower Gini coefficient. Consider saying 'at the 50% mark' in the option, or giving the shares at several points.

check.summary: Card and question a are correct. Question b and its why treat one point on the Lorenz curve as deciding the whole curve and the Gini coefficient, which is not strictly true because curves can cross.
